approach: Find the constant speed of the tip, the angle it sweeps in 15 s, and then the magnitude of the vector difference between the initial and final velocity.

steps.text: Find the angular speed of the seconds hand and the speed of its tip.
steps.equation: ω = 2π/60 = π/30 rad/s, v = ωr = π/30 cm/s

steps.text: Find the angle swept by the tip in 15 s.
The velocity vector keeps the same magnitude but turns through 90°, so find the magnitude of the vector difference between two perpendicular vectors of equal length.
Substitute v = π/30 cm/s to get the change in velocity.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming that because the speed (magnitude of velocity) stays constant, the velocity itself does not change, giving zero instead of accounting for the change in direction.
Using the chord formula without the factor of two, computing v sin(Δθ/2) instead of 2v sin(Δθ/2), which gives π/(30√2) cm/s.
